Denmark’s most popular museum of modern art has got it going on. As lights and colours play a major role this February, it works as a perfect excuse to go see the beloved KUSAMA installation – *Gleaming lights of the souls* – one of Kusama’s 12 infinity room creations, and one of the most popular installations at the Louisiana Museum of Modern Art. The room consists of a single space, with walls and ceilings covered in mirrors and a hundred lamps resembling glowing ping pong balls, constantly changing colour. Entering this room will truly make you feel as if you have entered a world without physical limitations. The installation is currently closed, but will reopen soon.

…

**ARoS Aarhus Art Museum**

How does a ten-story building, packed with modern and contemporary art, sound to you? With 20,700 square meters, ARoS is one of the largest art museums in Northern Europe – and it’s got plenty to offer! ARoS features 4 spacious galleries, a focus gallery and a whole story of installations. Indeed, make sure you end your visit on ARoS’ rainbow rooftop, Your Rainbow Panorama, which offers the best view over Denmark’s second largest city. The panorama offers a truly amazing experience, enabling you to see the city through different kinds of light and colours. Designmuseum Danmark
Located on Bredgade – the city’s main street for art and design galleries –
the museum features permanent exhibitions of Danish mid-century furniture
classics as well as heritage collections of decorative art.

The museum is dedicated to modern art and design and features the nation’s largest collection of mid-century
Danish chair design. The museum also exhibits Arne Jacobsen’s prefab summer cottage and other design classics.

Designed by Steven Holl, the museum is located in Herning, one of Denmark’s most thriving
industrial towns, and is part of a grand masterplan for the city’s art centres.

[Experience the best Danish architecture > ARKEN Museum of Modern Art]

Take a trip south of Copenhagen to the seaside art museum, ARKEN Museum of Modern Art. Designed by Danish architect Søren Robert Lund, ARKEN Museum of Modern Art opened in 1996. You can enjoy collections by Danish, Scandinavian and international artists at ARKEN.

…

[Experience the best Danish architecture > ARoS Art Museum]

ARoS Art Museum is a cultural hub in the dynamic city of Aarhus. You can easily recognise ARoS on Aarhus' skyline, thanks to the stunning installation on its roof, Your Rainbow Panorama, created by the artist Olafur Eliasson. Take a walk through Your Rainbow Panorama for unique views of Aarhus.

[Danish Design & Architecture]

Louisiana Museum of Modern Art
This world-famous art museum hosts changing exhibitions ensuring no
two visits are alike. The setting in itself makes the trip worthwhile with
stunning vistas of the Sound and the Swedish coast.

Designmuseum Danmark
Located on Bredgade – the city’s main street for art and design galleries –
the museum features permanent exhibitions of Danish mid-century furniture
classics as well as heritage collections of decorative art.

…

Trapholt Museum
The museum is dedicated to modern art and design and features the nation’s largest collection of mid-century
Danish chair design. The museum also exhibits Arne Jacobsen’s prefab summer cottage and other design classics.

…

HEART Museum of Contemporary Art
Designed by Steven Holl, the museum is located in Herning, one of Denmark’s most thriving
industrial towns, and is part of a grand masterplan for the city’s art centres.

…

ARoS Museum of Modern Art
The museum is crowned by a rainbow skywalk by artist Olafur
Eliasson. Opening in 2019 is a new underground extension with
an art installation by James Turrell. The museum is one of
Scandinavia’s largest and most-visited art museums.
